title: Neutral composable canvas capability and product-owned presentation
objective: Record and implement the owner rule that reusable packages provide neutral mechanisms, contracts, mount points, and replaceable defaults while products compose node components, edge presentations, effects, surface styling, and interaction choices without vendor-type leakage or graph-logic duplication.
validations: DEC-052 and accepted ADR-0014 record the owner rule and amend DEC-049 without changing Rust graph authority under DEC-051
source scan confirms x6-canvas has no @grafting/ui dependency, Card, product palette, product role, or fixed edge theme
pnpm.cmd nx run-many -t check test build --projects=ui,x6-canvas,architecture-studio --skip-nx-cache: all three checks and 25 tests passed; initial dependent Wasm build was sandbox-blocked only
pnpm.cmd nx run architecture-studio:build --skip-nx-cache outside the sandbox: Rust/Wasm, UI, x6-canvas, and Vite production build passed
production build: 1,190.44 kB raw / 354.20 kB gzip JS, 3.90 kB Worker, and 196.01 kB Wasm
ui and x6-canvas intentional API baselines were regenerated, reviewed, then normal api-check passed with no forbidden vendor module leakage
pnpm.cmd docs:check passed: repo map, artifact manifest, Graph IR, Rust API, and x6-canvas API are current
pnpm.cmd audit --prod outside the restricted network sandbox: no known vulnerabilities found
pnpm.cmd ai:check passed for 25 task records and pnpm.cmd ai:audit passed after regenerating derived task evidence
HTTP probe returned 200 for http://127.0.0.1:4511; automated visual acceptance was unavailable because this session exposed no in-app browser backend
risks: This intentionally changes the consumed x6-canvas public API and requires an atomic consumer and baseline migration.
A generic contract must not become a mirror of X6 configuration or a second graph/layout engine.
DOM lifecycle callbacks need deterministic disposal to avoid leaked React roots when canvas cells are removed.
Configurable defaults must remain replaceable and must not silently become product policy.
The Studio JavaScript bundle remains above the provisional 200 KiB gzip budget because of the current Ant Design/X6 composition; optimization needs a separate measured task.
Visual geometry, pan, and click behavior still require owner browser acceptance because no in-app browser backend was available.
DEC-033 still requires an independent reviewer before commit; this completion record is implementation evidence, not self-approval.
